```yaml
name: Test Count

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master, develop ]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  count-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      actions: read

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      timeout-minutes: 2

    - name: Set up Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v4
      with:
        python-version: "3.10"
      timeout-minutes: 3

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade --timeout 120 --retries 5 pip
        pip install --timeout 120 --retries 5 pytest
        pip install --timeout 120 --retries 5 -e .
      timeout-minutes: 5

    - name: Count tests
      id: count
      run: |
        python -c "
import os
import json
import subprocess

def count_test_functions():
    try:
        # Run pytest with --collect-only to get all test items
        result = subprocess.run([
            'pytest', 
            '--collect-only', 
            '--quiet',
            '--tb=no'
        ], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
        
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise Exception(f'Pytest collection failed: {result.stderr}')
            
        lines = result.stdout.split('\n')
        test_count = 0
        for line in lines:
            if line.strip().startswith('test_') or line.strip().startswith('def test_'):
                test_count += 1
                
        return test_count
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'Error counting tests: {e}')
        return 0

def format_number(num):
    if num >= 1000000:
        return f'{num/1000000:.1f}M'
    elif num >= 1000:
        return f'{num/1000:.1f}K'
    else:
        return str(num)

test_count = count_test_functions()
formatted_count = format_number(test_count)

# Write to test-stats.json
stats = {
    'count': test_count,
    'formatted': formatted_count
}

with open('test-stats.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(stats, f)

print(f'Test count: {test_count}')
print(f'Formatted count: {formatted_count}')
print(f'::set-output name=count::{test_count}')
print(f'::set-output name=formatted::{formatted_count}')
"
      timeout-minutes: 5

    - name: Update README with test count badge
      run: |
        # Read current README content
        README_CONTENT=$(cat README.md)
        
        # Create badge markdown
        BADGE_MARKDOWN="[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-${{ steps.count.outputs.formatted }}-brightgreen)](https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex/actions/workflows/test-count.yml)"
        
        # Find where to insert the badge (after existing badges)
        # Look for the first line that contains a badge or the start of badges section
        INSERT_POSITION=$(echo "$README_CONTENT" | grep -n -E "(^\[!\[.*\]\(.*\)\]|^##.*Test|^\s*$$|^\s*$)" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
        
        if [ -z "$INSERT_POSITION" ]; then
            INSERT_POSITION=1
        fi
        
        # Insert badge after the first line that looks like a badge or starts a badges section
        # If no such line found, insert at beginning
        if [ "$INSERT_POSITION" -eq 1 ]; then
            # Insert at the beginning of the file
            echo "$BADGE_MARKDOWN" > temp_readme.md
            cat README.md >> temp_readme.md
            mv temp_readme.md README.md
        else
            # Insert after the first badge-like line
            LINE_NUM=$((INSERT_POSITION + 1))
            sed -i "${LINE_NUM}i $BADGE_MARKDOWN" README.md
        fi
        
        # Alternative approach: insert after the first line that contains a badge
        # This is more robust for detecting existing badges
        if ! grep -q "!\[.*\]" README.md; then
            # No badges found, insert at beginning
            echo "$BADGE_MARKDOWN" > temp_readme.md
            cat README.md >> temp_readme.md
            mv temp_readme.md README.md
        else
            # Insert after first badge line
            FIRST_BADGE_LINE=$(grep -n "!\[.*\]" README.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
            if [ -n "$FIRST_BADGE_LINE" ]; then
                sed -i "${FIRST_BADGE_LINE}a $BADGE_MARKDOWN" README.md
            else
                # Fallback to beginning
                echo "$BADGE_MARKDOWN" > temp_readme.md
                cat README.md >> temp_readme.md
                mv temp_readme.md README.md
            fi
        fi
        
        # More precise approach: find the first line with a badge and insert after it
        # But also handle case where there might be no badges at all
        if grep -q "!\[.*\]" README.md; then
            # Find first badge line and insert after it
            FIRST_BADGE=$(grep -n "!\[.*\]" README.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
            if [ -n "$FIRST_BADGE" ]; then
                sed -i "${FIRST_BADGE}a $BADGE_MARKDOWN" README.md
            else
                # Insert at beginning if no proper badge found
                echo "$BADGE_MARKDOWN" > temp_readme.md
                cat README.md >> temp_readme.md
                mv temp_readme.md README.md
            fi
        else
            # No badges exist, insert at beginning
            echo "$BADGE_MARKDOWN" > temp_readme.md
            cat README.md >> temp_readme.md
            mv temp_readme.md README.md
        fi
        
        # Ensure we have a newline at the end of the file
        echo "" >> README.md
      timeout-minutes: 2

    - name: Commit changes
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
      run: |
        git config --local user.email "action@github.com"
        git config --local user.name "GitHub Action"
        git add README.md test-stats.json
        git commit -m "Update test count badge" || echo "No changes to commit"
      timeout-minutes: 2

    - name: Push changes
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
      uses: ad-m/github-push-action@master
      with:
        github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.ref }}
      timeout-minutes: 2

    - name: Upload test stats
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: test-stats
        path: test-stats.json
        retention-days: 90
      timeout-minutes: 2
```
